subject: Clarify IP origin & usage redlines for Order Form
content:

Cc: contracts@acme-dataworks.com

Subject: Re: Order Form — IP carveouts and training usage (redlines attached)

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redlined Order Form (Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx) and a short PDF that highlights the training exceptions we need for regulated datasets (exhibitA-training-exceptions.pdf).

High-level: we need clarity that (1) output generated by your hosted models that contains or derives from our proprietary data is assignable to Acme (we're seeking assignment on productized output), and (2) Acme retains right to opt datasets out of model training.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept assignment of customer-generated output in the Order Form? If not, would a long-form license plus an explicit no-training-without-consent clause work?

We'd like to close the contract this week. If you prefer, we can accept DocuSign routing once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Sarah Miller
Head of Procurement
Acme Dataworks

On Tue, May 23, 2028 at 09:40 AM laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 09:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form — IP carveouts and training usage (redlines attached)

Sarah — thanks for sending these over and for the quick timeline. Looping in Priyom (legal operations lead) and Ben (sales lead) to confirm commercial impact and final language. Olga, can you review the redlines below and advise on risk?

Quick read: Acme is asking for two main items that affect product/risk posture:
- Assignment of "productized output" (they've proposed language assigning ownership of model outputs that incorporate their proprietary data).
- Explicit opt-out for model training and related telemetry/feedback use (they want a hard opt-out applying to hosted and dedicated deployments).

Our position options (high-level):
1) Accept limited assignment for "derivative works" where output is a verbatim transformation of customer content (narrow, but sometimes acceptable for vertical customers).
2) Offer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable license for output + option to restrict use for model training unless customer opts in.
3) If assignment is unacceptable, offer stronger contractual protections: covenant not to use Acme data/outputs to train models; indemnity carveouts; audit rights; and a higher operational fee.

Olga — draft preferred redline language for option #2 (license + no-training-without-consent) and include a short fallback for assignment limited to "non-ML transformed product deliverables." If assignment is requested as-is, flag the areas we cannot accept without exec approval.

Ben — if we go with option #2, what's the uplift price/discount tradeoff we can offer? Also confirm whether Dedicated deployments change the tradeoff (we generally can be more flexible on training when customers run in their VPC).

I'll compile responses and come back to Sarah with a single proposal.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 23, 2028 at 11:04 AM priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme-dataworks.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 11:04:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form — IP carveouts and training usage (redlines attached)

Laura / team — quick operational/legal read. I like Laura's option #2 as a balanced path. Below are concrete redline suggestions we can propose to Acme to close this quickly:

1) Output: "Customer Output" means any output generated by the Service that contains or is derived from Customer Data. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, transferable license to Customer Output for Customer's internal and commercial use. For model productization (i.e., where Customer Output becomes an item for resale embedded in a product), parties agree to negotiate assignment on a case-by-case basis and Redwood will not withhold assignment solely on the basis of use of a Redwood core model.

2) Training/Data Use: Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train or improve Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent. For hosted deployments, Customer may choose either (a) an opt-in model (default) or (b) an opt-out control (if purchased as an add-on) that prevents Customer Data from entering Redwood training pipelines. For Dedicated and Private deployments, default behavior will exclude Customer Data from Redwood central training unless otherwise agreed.

3) Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable license to use anonymized feedback and telemetry to detect service incidents and to implement bug fixes and performance improvements; such usage will exclude training signal ingestion for model weight updates unless Customer provides consent.

4) Evidence & Audit: For regulated datasets, Customer may provide an Exhibit A with a list of protected datasets. Redwood will maintain an audit log of training exclusion requests and provide evidence upon reasonable request (subject to a standard confidentiality agreement).

Operational notes: implementing the opt-out add-on requires tagging pipelines and an audit surface. We should price this as a recurring security/compliance add-on. Ben — propose an uplift figure and I'll include it in the reply.

Olga — please redline the clauses above into Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx and return; call out any problematic words (e.g., "assignment" and "derivative") that may create precedent.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Policy
Redwood Inference
